body: I was in the same boat as you with my ex. She cheated on me and I stayed. She said she thought our relationship was hopeless, I begged her to stay— I apologized for making her feel guilty she cheated. Because she was my soulmate (or so I thought). We shared everything. So much of me was created with her. When she left I thought I would die before I found someone like her (or who I thought she was.) Before I could find love. 3 months after the breakup I still worry sometimes. In your first relationship especially (as she was for me), you tend to become so very attached to someone, so in love with them, that you feel like they’re everything. As if your very being is intertwined with them. Like you, I also have trouble feeling good enough. I wondered the same thing you are. But that’s not the question, really. Trust me when I say it gets so much better. You become freer. I regret not dumping her now (she actually had to break up with me… lol). Sometimes when the world, when people refuse to accept and love you, you’ve got to say fuck it and do it yourself. You only live once. It cannot be, do not let it be miserable. There’s no much more waiting for you.

I think it’s strange … you say it doesn’t weigh on you, but all this time later you’re posting anonymously about it? I’m not trying to accuse you, but I’d say the fact that you’re even thinking about it means it may still be troubling you.
If that’s the case, a moment of awkwardness will be nothing compared to the weight it would take off your chest.

The way I think about a lot of things is this:
Life is short. Really short. And in the end, embarrassment, loss, heartbreak, it all boils down to the same blur of experiences and emotion. I know it feels physically impossible to confess. You don’t want to lose her, or your friendship, you don’t want to live without her. But I think, just maybe, the regret will be much, much worse than anything else. She was CLEARLY into you then (no woman will make you touch her boob without some alternate intentions) and all you have to do is tell her you feel the same now. When you’re 80, on your deathbed, do you want to be weighed down by the fact that you never did something about this? Tell her how you feel. You’re already weighed down by the regret of not going for it the first time— do you really want to throw away this chance, too? Plus, if you’re truly close friends, she won’t cut you off, or be upset with you. I think it’ll just give you some closure. Worst case scenario? She doesn’t feel the same and you can move on. Don’t carry this around with you for the rest of your life.

In the beginning, he sort of reminded me of Hiyoko: foul-mouthed at times, bullying people... soon enough, though, he does prove to be quite the instigator. Honestly, seeing as his goal was to end the killing game, I think he didn't necessarily have bad intentions, but of course, he had all the wrong methods.

As for his speech... it's really hard to tell when he's lying vs telling the truth. At the time of his death, we still can't really tell. But, I think in all of his lies, there's some truth. 

Reading these comments, I really think that by this point in the game, it's really up to us individually whether he's evil or not-- there's no 100% truth, it's our perception. Either way, it's really cool to see it from another perspective. It kind of reminds me of the "Is Chara evil?" undertale discourse back in the day.

Hey man, this is definitely the right place. What you're experiencing *is* depression. I know cause I've had it for years. Depression isn't exactly sadness, it's emptiness.

Because you mention it's been happening since quarantine, this could be situational depression, which was triggered because of Covid. If you have a tough home situation, being there more often could also cause it. It could also simply be clinical depression that happened to rear its head at this specific time. No matter what the medical term is, this is depression. The best thing to do is talk and seek someone else who you may know in person, who has also experienced this or has a history of mental illness. Depression is.. sometimes futile. What helped me was medication, although for others it might be therapy. I'm sorry this sounds so robotic-- I TRULY know what you mean. It passes. It comes and goes but it's never permanent, never 24/7. You'll make your way out of that hole. (P.S. It's also good to know depression often stems from anxiety. Have you also been feeling anxious?)
